Housing here runs to a median build year of 1962, and 72.8 percent of the 2,016 units in Robbins predate 1980. 4.8 percent are prewar. Age is the first thing worth knowing about a house before it gets quoted, and it is the thing most quotes skip.

Behind the housing are 1,011 owner households and 544 renter households, 65 percent owner occupied. Of the units themselves, 23.4 percent are in buildings of two or more, 6 percent share a party wall as townhomes or rowhouses, and 70.6 percent stand on their own at a median 5.7 rooms. Median home value is $114,200.

Three figures put Robbins a long way from the average of the 76 places on this site: prewar housing at 4.8 percent against a 15.8 percent average, townhomes and rowhouses at 6 percent against a 7.5 percent average and housing in buildings of two or more at 23.4 percent against a 29 percent average.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Lead-safe work on Robbins houses

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 72.8 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Robbins. Housing that old falls under the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule, which covers any work disturbing paint in a home built before 1978. Illinois is not an authorized state for it, so EPA runs it here directly.

What it changes is the front and the back of a Robbins job, not the middle: plastic and sealed openings before, a specific cleanup standard after. It starts at roughly six square feet of disturbed paint per room inside, twenty square feet outside, and always on window replacement.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Robbins.

None of that is a reason to leave a Robbins house unpainted. It is a reason to know what the setup looks like before anyone opens a sander, and to hear it from the person doing the work rather than from a website.

Nothing on this page should be read as a certification claim. The slot for it below is empty because it has not been supplied, and an empty slot is more use to a homeowner in Robbins than a filled-in one nobody checked.

Robbins against its nearest neighbor

Put Robbins next to Midlothian, 1.5 miles away, and the housing does not match. The gaps are owner households (1,011 against 4,503); prewar share (4.8 percent against 11 percent); median home value ($114,200 against $200,300).

Why two houses in Robbins do not price the same

Interiors from around 1962 run to lower ceilings and more doors than a modern plan, and Robbins averages 5.7 rooms a unit. Six-panel doors, full baseboard runs and heavy casing: trim is where an interior job gets long. It is also the line most quotes leave vague, so ask for it on its own. 1,011 households own in Robbins and 544 rent, which produces two different phone calls. One wants the house to look right for ten years. The other wants a unit clean and let by the first of the month. Both are real work and neither should be quoted like the other.

What an estimate here has to account for

  • Containment, not just paint. 72.8 percent of housing in Robbins was built before 1980, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Whole elevations. 70.6 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.
  • Distance, stated. Robbins is 8.4 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Robbins is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is ranch, raised ranch and split-level, usually masonry to the sill line with frame gables above. Almost all the exterior paint in Robbins sits above head height, which is why the work takes longer than the surface area suggests.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1962 median build year, and the split between 70.6 percent detached houses, 6 percent attached homes and 23.4 percent in buildings of two units or more.

An inference, not a measurement. Neither the Census nor the regional housing data records what a wall in Robbins is made from, so no percentage is attached to it and none should be. Your own elevation settles it in four seconds from the sidewalk.

Questions

Asked about Robbins

Is the $114,200 median home value in Robbins what a job here costs?

No. That figure describes the houses, not the work. $114,200 is what the Census estimates a home in Robbins is worth, and it earns its place on this page because value tracks size and age, which is what a painter is actually pricing. There is no price list on this site because there is no honest local one to publish yet.

Who actually shows up in Robbins?

Mike Walsh owns the company, walks the job and stays on it while our crew works. Call 708-935-4289. It is worth saying because on a job this size the gap between whoever measured it and whoever turns up is where most of the disappointment comes from.

Can it be done a room at a time?

Yes, and on 5.7-room housing it is often the right call. Doing one room properly beats doing four at a pace that shows, and it spreads the cost across seasons rather than across a credit card. Say that is what you want when you call, because it changes how the work is sequenced.

What changes the price most on a house here?

Prep. Housing here runs to a 1962 median, which means several coats are already on the woodwork and some of them were put on badly. Undoing that is the expensive part, and it is the part that a fast number leaves out and a slow one explains.
